pr.title: Polish Bit setup: optional folder when adding a repository, setup shortcuts
pr.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jasondwhyte"} -->
_Requested by **Jason** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01YGtEMFvZnSp5cxW5MGErkd?thread=cmsg_01YGtEMFvZnSp5cxW5MGErkd4yrx42V2CNrsAy6nSKB54b)_

Before: adding a repository in **Repositories** required the path to a clone already on the computer. That meant cloning it yourself first, and it couldn't be done from a phone. Bit's **Help me set up** (#73) was only reachable from Bit's page.

After: the folder is optional when adding a repository. Leave it empty, and the save button reads **Download and connect**: Orbit downloads its own copy with the GitHub CLI, keeps it up to date, and connects it. If Bit already downloaded a copy, Orbit uses that one. This works from a browser too. The empty inbox and the empty Repositories page offer **Set up with Bit** (using Bit's chosen name), which opens Bit's page and asks **Help me set up**. Bit's own page, with no notes yet and Orbit not set up, offers the same button.

This finishes the polish part of stage 2 of epic #30.

How:
- `Engine::own_copy` is the download step pulled out of Bit's connect button: it downloads beside the target, then moves the copy into place, under `cloning`. `setup::carry_on` runs work in a task of its own, so it continues if the window goes away.
- `save_repository` uses both for a new repository with an empty path. It refuses a repository that's already connected before downloading anything, sets `keep_updated`, and then validates and saves as before. Bit's follow-up note from #73 fires as for any new repository.
- In the Repositories dialog, the path is required only when editing. With it empty, "Keep this clone up to date" shows on and locked. The demo does the same.
- Tests: an engine test for download-and-connect (including the Bit follow-up, adding it again without downloading, a failed download, and an existing repository still needing its folder), app tests for the dialog and for "Set up with Bit" from the empty inbox (with commands shown as code). The user guide, architecture notes and README are updated.

Checks run: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --no-default-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --no-default-features` (426 passed), `npx prettier --check .`, `npx eslint .`, `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`, `npx vitest run` (185 passed), `npx vite build`.

## Milo PR review
**CHANGES REQUESTED**

Repository: analogproblems/orbit #74  
Head: `867276bfba41e1b2bcd833e92ac821a94af8ad87`

### Findings
**F1 · P2 · [src-tauri/src/engine/settings.rs:100–107](https://github.com/analogproblems/orbit/blob/867276bfba41e1b2bcd833e92ac821a94af8ad87/src-tauri/src/engine/settings.rs#L100-L107): keep the entire download-and-connect operation alive after request cancellation.**
Only `own_copy` runs inside `carry_on`. Checkout validation, saving the repository settings, and the connected notification still run in the requesting `save_repository` future. The remote command handler awaits that future directly. If the browser disconnects or closes while cloning, cancellation drops the outer future: the detached clone finishes, but the repository is never connected or persisted. This is especially relevant to a long download initiated from a phone. The existing setup path detaches the complete setup operation.

Move the complete validated save/connect operation into the cancellation-independent task, preserving serialization and duplicate checks. Add a regression test with a gated fake clone: cancel the caller while cloning, release the clone, then assert that settings and the connected notification are committed. Current new tests await the save normally and do not cover this interruption. This finding is based on static control-flow review; native cancellation behavior was not executed locally.

### Scope and verification
Reviewed all 12 complete changed-file patches, repository guidance, relevant frontend/backend source, tests and discussions. Scope included empty-path cloning, checkout validation, duplicate/persistence handling, setup entry points, loading/demo behavior and documentation. No additional suggestions.

Observed GitHub: open, non-draft and mergeable without conflict at posting check. No check runs, commit statuses or Actions runs were present for the head or verified synthetic merge `8d86feab9a716d835d13269cebd0737755d15808`. Empty combined-status “pending” is not an observed running job. No CI pass is claimed. Rulesets were empty; detailed branch-protection visibility was unavailable (403), so required-check/review requirements are not fully visible.

**Executed on TESTBOX, head only:** 185 tests passed across 20 files; no failed or skipped tests reported. Dependency download and test exits 0; OOM=false and timeout=false for both. Preparation, service stop and bounded cleanup exited 0. Native/Rust, browser, build, lint/typecheck, other integration tiers and production/provider calls were not run.

Immutable configured and observed node24 image: `sha256:64af3819f9275802414d7cdc38c27e9d82bd564dec4d4da87d008255d36c63b4`.

Exact commands, with ROOT and RUN defined:
```sh

RUN=$ROOT/runs/orbit/867276bfba41-db4db373
IMAGE=sha256:64af3819f9275802414d7cdc38c27e9d82bd564dec4d4da87d008255d36c63b4

python "$ROOT/isolated.py" "$RUN" npm-download --image "$IMAGE" --purpose download --network bridge 'npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund'
python "$ROOT/isolated.py" "$RUN" npm-test --image "$IMAGE" 'npm test -- --maxWorkers=2'
python "$ROOT/services.py" stop "$RUN"
python "$ROOT/cleanup.py" "$RUN"
```
Both stop and cleanup ran in host finally handling. Before execution: UID/GID 1000, zero capabilities, no-new-privileges, read-only root, 2 CPUs, 4 GiB RAM, 512 PIDs, bounded temporary storage; only task-owned writable paths, Git metadata read-only, no host credentials/SSH agent/Docker socket or published ports. Networking was enabled only for download with lifecycle scripts disabled; tests had network none and no external routes. Trusted Git with no external diff/text conversion verified the exact head and clean tracked/index state before and after each stage.

Evidence retained under RUN: `revision.json`, `results/{prepare.log,npm-download.log,npm-test.log,*.result.json,*.isolation.json,*.docker-observed.json,supervisor.json,cleanup.json}`. Container artifact directory `RUN/artifacts` was retained and empty. No source checkout changes, global prune or source reset. **F1 fixed in 0db1179.** `save_repository` now runs the whole save in its own task through `carry_on`: the download, checkout validation, the settings commit and Bit's follow-up note. commit.message:
Finish connecting a downloaded repository even if the caller goes away

Adding a repository without a folder ran only the download in its own
task, so a browser that closed mid-download left the copy downloaded
but never connected. The whole save now runs in its own task, holding
the download lock until the repository is connected, as Bit's Connect
button does. A test closes the caller mid-download and checks the
repository still connects with Bit's follow-up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01EDJU2uY2NCz6Ch7CDHNcNA

Polish Bit setup: optional folder when adding a repository, setup shortcuts

- Adding a repository with no local folder now downloads Orbit's own
  copy with the GitHub CLI, kept up to date, through the same download
  Bit's Connect button uses. It works from a browser too, and carries on
  if the window closes.
- The empty inbox and Repositories page offer "Set up with Bit", and
  Bit's empty page offers Help me set up while Orbit isn't set up.
